ei.title: Why Two Reasons Are Worse Than One
ei.subject: 올림포스전국연합고1_2026

fullPassage: My colleagues and I ran an experiment testing two different messages meant to convince thousands of resistant alumni to make a donation. One message emphasized the opportunity to do good: donating would benefit students, faculty, and staff. The other emphasized the opportunity to feel good: donors would enjoy the warm glow of giving. The two messages were equally effective: in both cases, 6.5 percent of the unwilling alumni ended up donating. Then we combined them, because two reasons are better than one. Except they weren't. When we put the two reasons together, the giving rate dropped below 3 percent. Each reason alone was more than twice as effective as the two combined. The audience was already skeptical. When we gave them different kinds of reasons to donate, we triggered their awareness that someone was trying to persuade them — and they shielded themselves against it.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

❌ ③ combined: 과거시제, 정상
❌ ④ dropped: 과거시제, 정상
det.tip: messages (meant to convince) = 설득하도록 의도된 메시지 (과거분사)
